$comment: The Tavern frontend gate's contract. Authority for the obligations: the surface declarations below, executed by dialogue-web/tests/frontend-criteria.ts (the design document they used to cite, design/architecture/tavern-frontend-criteria.md, is not in the mounted design corpus - the citation was dropped rather than kept dangling). This file is what makes a frontend requirement impossible to delete quietly: the surface list here must equal the identities the shell entry accepts, the corpus is the mounted journey directory itself, the corpus must not fall below its floor, every declared criterion must be exercised, and a disabled test fails the gate instead of reducing it. No suite file is named here, so a deleted spec cannot be declared and a renamed, re-added or newly written one joins the gate on its own; the credential journey list is empty because the two provider journeys the removed companion-turn suite carried have no home yet (reported by the release lane, not silently dropped).

surfaceInventory.rule: Every profile identity the shell entry accepts is a surface: the gate derives them from the entry itself and requires this file to declare exactly those, so adding a pane without declaring it fails, and so does declaring a pane that no longer exists.

corpus.rule: The corpus is the whole mounted journey directory - the same corpus the release lane's test:mounted zone runs - so nothing here names a suite file and no file list can rot into suites that do not exist. The gate requires every journey file in the directory to appear in the run, the run to hold no journey from outside it, and the run to hold at least minimumTests rows; the floor is a body guard (the corpus holds 133 rows today) so gutting the corpus fails even while the criteria test and the headline journeys below still exist.

surfaces.criteriaTitle: conformance: the product surface meets the frontend criteria

requiredTitles: conformance: the product surface meets the frontend criteria
composed profile redeems once, renders nested Chat and redacted Game, then reloads from composed state
the mounted conversation stops an armed reply, keeps the stop durable across a reload, and sends again
the composed conversation opens the projected event stream, previews a delta, and recovers through authoritative state once per resync
choosing a character card file imports it in one action, and reports what the Host kept and could not use
the product Characters surface owns the world book and binds through world-info.bind with the authoritative revision
the product Chats surface renames through chat/title and moves the conversation heading from the composed state
the product Settings surface shows the real settings panels and moves both languages
the product Settings surface creates, tests and activates a connection whose API key never reaches the document
Game STOP is generation-bound, single-flight, rereads stopped, and remains independent from Chat Stop
Game Resume is generation-bound and single-flight, rereads authoritative state, and renders no synthetic completion
Game endgame requires an explicit confirm before the POST and reaches the terminal route once
confirms a safe candidate and rereads authoritative state
gate 1: the shell is anchored to the viewport at seven sizes on every surface
gate 4: Tab reaches every AppBar entry, Enter opens a surface, Escape returns to the conversation
gate 5: no console error, page error or failed API response while opening every surface
the shipped shell fills the viewport in both axes, at every size
